report:
### Conclusion
The health claim that consuming more olive oil reduces stroke risk is supported by scientific evidence rather than false. Randomized controlled trials, systematic reviews, and meta-analyses consistently link higher olive oil consumption to reduced stroke incidence.

### Summary of Evidence
* **Randomized Controlled Trials:** The PREDIMED trial showed that a Mediterranean diet supplemented with extra-virgin olive oil significantly reduced major cardiovascular events, specifically stroke, in individuals at high risk (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29897866/).
* **Systematic Reviews:** A systematic review on dietary patterns and stroke prevention found that higher olive oil intake significantly lowered stroke risk (RR: 0.60, 95% CI: 0.47–0.77) (https://www.academia.edu/109593807/Diet_and_primary_prevention_of_stroke_Systematic_review_and_dietary_recommendations_by_the_ad_hoc_Working_Group_of_the_Italian_Society_of_Human_Nutrition).
* **Meta-Analyses:** A meta-analysis of observational studies found that consuming two tablespoons (25 g) of olive oil daily was associated with a 26% lower risk of stroke (https://www.myolivea.com/blogs/research/olive-oil-stroke-cardiovascular-meta-analysis-2014).
* **Dietary Patterns:** A broader meta-analysis confirmed that adherence to the Mediterranean diet—in which olive oil serves as the primary fat source—significantly decreases stroke risk (HR: 0.88, 95% CI: 0.84–0.91) (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39777701/).

In summary, clinical trial and epidemiological evidence demonstrates that higher olive oil consumption contributes to a lower risk of stroke.
